_readme: Consumption audit trail for UT-N (2026-09-08). Every template with a local consumer repo under C:\dev must list EVERY Type="Variable" Target it declares, each with a one-line citation of where the consuming repo actually reads and USES it (not just declares it). tests/test_variable_consumption.py enforces that the two lists (template vs. this file) match exactly, and that a template flagged no_local_consumer carries no per-var entries. This file does NOT re-derive consumption on its own (this repo's CI has no checkout of the private consumer repos) — it is the durable record of the audit a human/worker performed, so a Variable added without one is caught structurally instead of silently accreting. Every citation starts `reads <VARIABLE>`: the exact env-var name the code looks up, not just the feature it serves. For a pydantic-settings field that name is env_prefix + the field name (case-insensitive unless case_sensitive=True; an alias / validation_alias replaces it), so field backup_db_user with no prefix reads BACKUP_DB_USER, never DB_BACKUP_USER. A pydantic citation names a `field <name>`, and the test checks that every `field <name>` in a citation, and every lookup written as ${NAME}, os.environ.get('NAME'), os.environ['NAME'], getenv('NAME') or process.env.NAME, spells the Variable; other shapes, such as a project's own _env('NAME') wrapper, are not checked, and neither are env_prefix, aliases or case_sensitive=True, since no consumer uses them. If the name the code looks up is not the Variable, the Variable is read by nothing: fix the template, not the citation. Re-measure and update the citation whenever the corresponding line in the consumer repo moves. Each template entry may also carry `paths` (one citation per Type="Path" Target, opening `reads <PATH>`, checked exactly like Variables) and `declared_for` (a Variable or Path the template declares for a later release or branch: the value names that package and what it reads, and does not claim a read today).

vars.OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL: reads OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL in https://github.com/ollama/ollama (main branch): envconfig/config.go NumParallel = Uint("OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL", 1); upstream's default is 1

paths./root/.ollama: reads /root/.ollama in https://github.com/ollama/ollama (main branch): envconfig/config.go Models() uses OLLAMA_MODELS when set and otherwise $HOME/.ollama/models; the Dockerfile sets no OLLAMA_MODELS, so the store is /root/.ollama when HOME is /root (inferred for the image's default user; verify on first start)

vars.KW_API_ORIGIN: reads KW_API_ORIGIN via {$KW_API_ORIGIN} in config/caddy/Caddyfile:118,131,150 (reverse_proxy to tape on the public, admin and consumer routes)
vars.KW_WEB_CLIENTS: reads KW_WEB_CLIENTS via {$KW_WEB_CLIENTS} in config/caddy/Caddyfile:95,116 (client_ip matcher for the keystone pages and tape's public paths)
vars.KW_ADMIN_CLIENTS: reads KW_ADMIN_CLIENTS via {$KW_ADMIN_CLIENTS} in config/caddy/Caddyfile:129 (client_ip matcher for tape's /v1/admin)
vars.KW_API_CLIENTS: reads KW_API_CLIENTS via {$KW_API_CLIENTS} in config/caddy/Caddyfile:85,148 (client_ip matcher for keystone-web's /api/health and tape's consumer API)

paths./etc/caddy: reads /etc/caddy via the Caddyfile inside it (/etc/caddy/Caddyfile): kw-edge config/caddy/README.md:7; scripts/validate_configs.sh:62

vars.KW_EGRESS_RULES_URL: reads KW_EGRESS_RULES_URL via kw-edge config/squid/sync/egress-sync.pl:46 (keystone's rules endpoint; entry.sh:20 starts the sync only when it is set)
vars.KW_EGRESS_TOKEN: reads KW_EGRESS_TOKEN via kw-edge config/squid/sync/egress-sync.pl:47 (the bearer token; entry.sh:30 unsets it before squid starts)
vars.KW_EGRESS_POLL_SECONDS: reads KW_EGRESS_POLL_SECONDS via kw-edge config/squid/sync/egress-sync.pl:54 (seconds between polls, 1 to 60; blank or out of range uses 30)

paths./etc/squid/kw/rules: reads /etc/squid/kw/rules via kw-edge config/squid/squid.conf:107 (include of rules.conf; entry.sh:11 seeds it and egress-sync.pl replaces it by rename)
paths./etc/squid/kw/sync: reads /etc/squid/kw/sync via kw-edge config/squid/sync/entry.sh:23 (runs egress-sync.pl from this directory)
paths./etc/squid/kw/exceptions: reads /etc/squid/kw/exceptions via kw-edge config/squid/squid.conf:117 (include of *.conf; squid fails the parse with no file)
paths./etc/squid/kw/operator-resolver.conf: reads /etc/squid/kw/operator-resolver.conf (a Path, not a Variable) via kw-edge config/squid/squid.conf:23 (include: the dns_nameservers line the proxy resolves through; an empty file keeps the container resolver)
paths./etc/squid/kw/destinations: reads /etc/squid/kw/destinations via kw-edge config/squid/squid.conf:50 (the per-source destination lists, one host-held file per source named <source>.allow; the lists are not in kw-edge)

vars.CLAMAV_NO_CLAMD: reads CLAMAV_NO_CLAMD via the clamav/clamav 1.5.4-debian image entrypoint (clamav-docker clamav/README-debian.md, 'Controlling the container': default false; true stops clamd from starting)

paths./var/lib/clamav: reads /var/lib/clamav via the clamav/clamav image: freshclam writes the signature databases to the database directory (clamav-docker clamav/README-debian.md, 'Controlling the container')

vars.CLAMAV_NO_FRESHCLAMD: reads CLAMAV_NO_FRESHCLAMD via the clamav/clamav 1.5.4-debian image entrypoint (clamav-docker clamav/README-debian.md, 'Controlling the container': default false; true stops the freshclam daemon from starting)

paths./var/lib/clamav: reads /var/lib/clamav via the clamav/clamav image: clamd loads the signature databases from the database directory (clamav-docker clamav/README-debian.md, 'Controlling the container'); mounted read-only here
paths./tmp: reads /tmp via clamd's scratch and socket paths: the image keeps clamd.sock in /tmp (clamav-docker clamav/README-debian.md, default socket /tmp/clamd.sock); the README does not name the scratch directory itself

vars.KB_TOKEN: reads KB_TOKEN in https://github.com/sdr-ventures/kb-service at v0.6.1: worker/ingest_worker.py:18 os.environ["KB_TOKEN"] (the bearer sent on every claim/result/fail call)
vars.POLL_SECONDS: reads POLL_SECONDS in https://github.com/sdr-ventures/kb-service at v0.6.1: worker/ingest_worker.py:19 os.environ.get("POLL_SECONDS", "30") (wait between empty claims)

vars.NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: reads NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES via the runtime, no app-code lookup: the NVIDIA container runtime reads it at container start to pick the GPUs; the worker then selects CUDAExecutionProvider when present (worker/ingest_worker.py:69, worker/Dockerfile:17-24 in https://github.com/sdr-ventures/kb-service at v0.9.5)
vars.NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES: reads NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES via the runtime, no app-code lookup: the NVIDIA container runtime reads it to decide which driver features reach the container; the CUDA libraries are installed at worker/Dockerfile:17-24 in https://github.com/sdr-ventures/kb-service at v0.9.5
